stem.text: A student prepares pentan-1-ol by the alkaline hydrolysis of 1-iodopentane. She gently warms the reaction mixture for 20 minutes.
When the student uses 1-chloropentane to prepare the same alcohol she has to change the condition of the reaction.
Which change in condition should she use and what is the correct reason for its use?

A.text: heat under reflux; $\text{C–Cl}$ bond is more polar than the $\text{C–I}$ bond

B.text: heat under reflux; $\text{C–Cl}$ bond is stronger than the $\text{C–I}$ bond

C.text: room temperature; $\text{C–Cl}$ bond is more polar than the $\text{C–I}$ bond

D.text: room temperature; $\text{C–Cl}$ bond is shorter than the $\text{C–I}$ bond

A: $\text{C–Cl}$ bond is more polar than the $\text{C–I}$ bond
B: $\text{C–Cl}$ bond is stronger than the $\text{C–I}$ bond
C: $\text{C–Cl}$ bond is more polar than the $\text{C–I}$ bond
D: $\text{C–Cl}$ bond is shorter than the $\text{C–I}$ bond
